findings.problem: Diverged is defined as 'local commits origin lacks', which also covers a branch only ahead of origin; right after the first trigger (a local merge, not pushed) the base is ahead, so the Local: line reports diverged every time; the Local: line has no ahead form.
findings.scenario: Track-back step 6 → sync → fetch: base holds the merge commit, origin has nothing new → step 4 reports 'diverged: <base> — N local / 0 remote commits'.
findings.closure: github.md defines diverged as commits on both sides; a branch only ahead is reported in the Local: line as 'ahead: <branch> — <n> local, not pushed', a form the Local: line lists; a contract case pins both.

findings.problem: Base branch checked out in another worktree: git refuses fetch <b>:<b>, outcome unstated; Q1 start-of-task fetch only implicit, not in ## Method; pr-assets clause only on the push path.
findings.scenario: Agent in a track worktree, main tree on the base: fetch origin base:base refused, agent improvises.

findings.problem: GS6 drops the whole Never line (a permissive clause on it passes); unpinned vigilance: never stashed, update-ref/branch -f ban, strictly behind, the two then-sync clauses; G20.001 near-duplicates G17.26, G20.002 weak pin.
findings.scenario: 'strictly behind' reworded to 'behind or diverged' stays green.

findings.problem: 'that ask is the user's, expected here' frames the hook ask as routine; the agent must not pre-announce it as just approve.
findings.scenario: Agent tells the user to approve the base-branch ask without showing what moves.
